subject.title: [RFC] Multi-Agent Collaboration Enhancement: Capability Profiling + Shared Blackboard + Layered Memory + Token Cost Governance

question: Which subset of the multi-agent collaboration stack, if any, should OpenClaw core own versus routing to plugins/ClawHub or narrower trackers?
rationale: The issue combines core runtime routing, memory visibility, persistent schemas, security boundaries, and budget enforcement, and current VISION.md both supports some foundation work and rejects heavy default orchestration layers.

options.title: Sponsor Narrow Core Foundations
options.body: Keep this RFC open and split accepted work into small core issues for missing seams such as safe performance metrics, blackboard API boundaries, or budget hooks after security review.

options.title: Route Full Stack To Plugins
options.body: Declare the end-to-end collaboration stack plugin/ClawHub territory and keep only missing plugin APIs or security/core hardening in this repo.

options.title: Supersede With Narrow Trackers
options.body: Close or supersede this broad RFC only if maintainers choose specific canonical follow-ups such as #65403 or post-#98536 access-control issues to own the remaining work.

recommendation.title: Sponsor Narrow Core Foundations
recommendation.body: Keep this RFC open and split accepted work into small core issues for missing seams such as safe performance metrics, blackboard API boundaries, or budget hooks after security review.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is the strongest available owner for the product-scope choice because the decision depends on VISION.md guardrails, related scoping comments, and agent-runtime history.
